title: Generative Realities — Dentsu Creative Trends 2026
overview: A trends report framing what’s trending, timely, and timeless amid an algorithm-accelerated culture cycle, highlighting cost-of-living pressures, declining social connectedness, and complex relationships with technology and nostalgia.

sections.title: Escape Velocity
sections.summary: Consumers seek escape from adult responsibilities through fantasies, fandoms, and ‘cuteification,’ with comfort tinged by uncertainty.

subsections.title: Fantastical Fandoms
subsections.summary: The power of immersive fictional universes.

data_points: 70% agree modern life is so stressful they need to escape; 63% say cute products/packaging bring joy; 36% define themselves by fandoms.

sections.title: Electric Dreams
sections.summary: As AI accelerates, emotional ties to AI deepen, ‘slop’ content rises, and slow, crafted media gains appeal; AI influencers raise ethics and disclosure questions.

subsections.title: AI-Influencers Assemble
subsections.summary: The ethics of hyper-realistic AI influencers.

data_points: 53% use AI-enabled chat in personal life; 51% ask it questions once asked of humans; 32% sometimes feel an AI chatbot understands them better than friends/family; 46% confident spotting AI content; 43% not interested in following AI influencers.
implications: Avoiding ‘workslop,’ prioritizing how interactions feel, and designing for difference at scale.

sections.title: Trad Lives
sections.summary: A turn to nature, hyperlocal living, and renewed spirituality; the countryside and craft re-emerge as aspirational.

subsections.title: The Land Grab
subsections.summary: A powerful desire to connect with the earth.

subsections.title: Spiritual Quests
subsections.summary: A newfound interest in religion and spirituality.

data_points: Examples span foraging, farmstays, gardening, and a rise in young National Trust members; brands and culture foreground soil, fungi, and fermentation.

sections.title: Alone Together
sections.summary: Loneliness and fragmentation spur new ways to socialize, NoLo ‘natural highs,’ and influencer/streamer roles as connective tissue.

subsections.title: Village People
subsections.summary: New forms of socializing rebuild the ‘village.’

subsections.title: Natural Highs
subsections.summary: New behaviors require new possibilities (e.g., NoLo, daytime raves).

subsections.title: Islands in the Stream
subsections.summary: Creators provide much-needed connection amid fragmented media.

implications: Everyday party people; Empower the connectors; Connections that count.

sections.title: Analog Futures
sections.summary: Younger generations embrace simpler, tactile devices and anti-algorithm strategies; nostalgia and craft regain cultural value.

subsections.title: Neo-Luddites
subsections.summary: The desire to disconnect from devices.

subsections.title: The Anti-Algorithm
subsections.summary: A search for taste, individuality, serendipity.

subsections.title: The Way We Were
subsections.summary: Nostalgia for simpler, more connected times.

data_points: 40% say the online world feels so stressful they try to switch off; 50% try to ration their own screen time.

conclusion: Macro forces—cost-of-living pressures, fragmentation, and AI acceleration—simultaneously intensify tech ties and drive reconnection with the outdoors and craft. To lead, solve for the trend behind the trend and win with the algorithm, not follow it.
